recent_articles.title: Liquor To Soon Be Available In Ladakh's Tourist Spots
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena** approved a new excise policy for **Ladakh**, allowing the sale of hard liquor in retail vends, guest houses, and homestays. The policy aims to curb drug dependence, optimize revenue, and improve tourism by expanding access to low-alcohol content liquor. Key reforms include permitting beer bars with micro-breweries, opening 20 new liquor vends through e-auction, and allowing liquor consumption within hotel premises.  The policy also simplifies licensing procedures, reduces the number of documents required, and introduces a uniform excise duty structure.

recent_articles.title: Traffic chaos near toll plaza leaves commuters stranded in Ganderbal
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Massive traffic jams** near toll plazas at Nagbal and Beehama on the Srinagar-Leh highway caused significant delays for commuters during the long weekend.  Commuters complained of hours-long waits, alleging inadequate traffic regulation and personnel deployment by authorities despite modern infrastructure. **Residents** demanded relocation of the toll plaza to a less congested area, citing its impact on public movement as a major bottleneck.  **Deputy Superintendent of Police (Traffic) Ganderbal**, Gulzar Ahmad, confirmed that concerns have been communicated to higher authorities for immediate action.

recent_articles.title: Ladakh's new excise policy eases restrictions on liquor sale
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Vinai Kumar Saxena**, the **Ladakh Lieutenant Governor**, approved a new Excise Policy, permitting the sale of hard liquor through retail vends and extending availability to four more districts. The policy also simplifies licensing procedures, reduces excise duty rates, and allows for beer bars and liquor sales within hotels.  The policy aims to curb illicit alcohol trade, promote tourism, and optimize revenue while supporting public welfare.

recent_articles.title: Who drinks the most? Arunachal tops national chart, Himachal leads North - The Tribune
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **National Family Health Survey (NFHS)-6** revealed that **Arunachal Pradesh** has the highest proportion of men aged 15 and above reporting alcohol consumption, at 50.5 percent.  In northern India, **Himachal Pradesh** leads in alcohol consumption among men with 30.2 percent reporting consumption. The survey also found that **Chandigarh** has the highest overweight or obese population among men, with 48.5 percent of men falling into this category.

recent_articles.title: J&K High Court upholds dismissal of policeman over militant links, reverses single judge verdict
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh** upheld the dismissal of a police constable, Ghulam Mohammad Tantray, accused of militant links. The court rejected a 2011 judgment that had quashed his termination from service, finding sufficient grounds for the government's decision to dispense with the departmental inquiry.  The government argued that conducting a regular inquiry would have compromised security interests and exposed witnesses to threats. **Mohsin S. Qadri**, Senior Additional Advocate General represented the government.

recent_articles.title: In travels of Buddha’s sacred relics, India’s soft power outreach | India News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Piprahwa relics**, a significant collection of Buddhist artifacts, arrived in Leh, Ladakh, drawing large crowds and causing traffic jams. This event is reminiscent of a 1950 exhibition that aimed to boost the morale of the local population after a conflict with Pakistan. **Sonam Wangchuk Shakspo**, a scholar and diplomat, notes that this display was part of a broader strategy by newly independent India to use Buddhist heritage for cultural diplomacy.  The relics have since been exhibited in various countries across Asia, including Sri Lanka, Mongolia, Singapore, South Korea, and Thailand.

recent_articles.title: How was FIR lodged 75 minutes before alleged recovery of weapons? J-K High Court seeks answers in terror case
recent_articles.sentiment_target: Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court** has raised concerns about the timeline of a 2019 terror case, noting that the FIR was filed 75 minutes before the alleged recovery of arms. The court observed that the original FIR was missing from the trial record and directed the government to inform it whether the investigating officer remains in service.  The court also requested the petitioner's counsel to provide a chronology of prosecution witnesses. **Sabeel Ahmad Baba**, along with two co-accused, remain under arrest as they seek bail in this case.

recent_articles.title: LG directs Ladakh Admin to adopt austerity measures as per PM's call
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Vinai Kumar Saxena**, the Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh, has issued directives to all departments to promote austerity and sustainable practices in line with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's call for a greener future. **Saxena** directed departments to reduce government expenditure, cut fuel consumption, promote renewable energy, encourage local products, and enhance environmental sustainability. He also emphasized the need for greater domestic tourism, natural farming, and efficient resource utilization across sectors. All departments have been asked to submit an action plan report within 30 days and launch public awareness campaigns on various sustainable initiatives.

recent_articles.title: Ladakh L-G Saxena launches ecological restoration project to reclaim 800 acres of barren land - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Lieutenant-Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena** launched an ambitious ecological restoration project in Ladakh, aiming to reclaim nearly 800 acres of barren land near Spituk. The project utilizes excess water from the recently restored Igoo-Phey irrigation canal to replenish depleted aquifers and trigger natural vegetation growth.  Officials believe this initiative will improve soil health, create opportunities for sustainable agriculture and afforestation, and contribute to long-term ecological benefits in the region. This project aligns with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of restoring 26 million hectares of degraded land by 2030.

recent_articles.title: Financial decisions will rest with elected leaders: Sonam Wangchuk on Ladakh’s agreement with Centre - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sonam Wangchuk**, a renowned climate activist, welcomed the agreement between the **Centre** and representatives of Ladakh Apex Body (LAB) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) which will see an elected Chief Minister for the Union Territory of Ladakh.  The decision grants the UT-level Assembly legislative power over budget allocation and bureaucracy control, with the elected representatives taking responsibility for financial decisions. The agreement also includes safeguards under Article 371 to protect environment, land, culture, and nature.

recent_articles.title: Centre promised more legislative powers for Ladakh, says delegation - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** proposed a new mechanism to grant **Ladakh** greater legislative, financial, and administrative powers within the existing Union Territory framework.  Civil society members who attended a sub-committee meeting with MHA officials on Friday (May 22, 2026) reported that the talks were positive and that the MHA would soon send a draft outlining the proposed changes.

recent_articles.title: Ladakh seeks belonging through representation - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Union Ministry of Home Affairs** argues that Ladakh needs more districts rather than a legislature due to its sparse population, strategic sensitivity, and financial dependence on the Centre. This argument is criticized as flawed and reflects an impoverished understanding of democracy, echoing historical paternalistic views by the British Empire.

recent_articles.title: Ladakh leaders to meet Home Ministry officials on May 22, Sonam Wangchuk part of delegation - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A delegation from Ladakh, including climate activist **Sonam Wangchuk**, is meeting with **Union Home Ministry** officials on Friday to discuss demands for constitutional safeguards such as Statehood and inclusion under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution. This meeting follows a previous inconclusive high-powered committee meeting in February and comes after the violence in Leh city in September 2025, which stalled talks.  The delegation will reiterate their demands for Statehood, while officials have offered safeguards under Article 371 of the Constitution.

recent_articles.title: ECI set to roll out phase III of SIR in ‘coming days’ to cover 22 States, UTs - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is set to begin phase three of its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list process in the coming days, covering nearly 40 crore electors across 17 states and five UTs.  This follows completion of SIR in 10 states and three UTs previously, which has successfully removed over 60 lakh deceased voters from the rolls. The ECI had initially delayed the rollout due to Assembly elections in several states but is now proceeding with the revision process.  The exercise aims to ensure accurate voter lists for upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: Congress seeks discussion in Parliament on China's 'support' to Pakistan in Operation Sindoor - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh demanded a discussion in Parliament on **China's** claims of providing on-site technical support to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor last year.  Ramesh questioned the government's loosening of investment and trade curbs on China, its deepening industrial dependency, and why Prime Minister Narendra Modi gave a clean chit to China in 2020 after the conflict. He cited **Lt. Gen. Rahul Singh**, Deputy Chief of Army Staff, who had previously revealed details about **China's** involvement.  Ramesh emphasized the need for these issues to be discussed in Parliament.

recent_articles.title: New invasive moth threatens Ladakh’s farm-based economy - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Scientists** in Ladakh have discovered a new species of moth, the **Phalera cf. bucephala**, in the Suru Valley. The larvae of this insect, known as the buff-tip moth, are voracious feeders and can cause significant damage to trees. This discovery has raised concerns about its potential impact on the local farm-based economy.

recent_articles.title: Census enumerators ID can be verified through QR code - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Lalit Jain**, Director of Census Operations (DCO), **Haryana**, has introduced QR code-enabled identity cards for enumerators to address concerns about authenticity.  Jain explained that residents can verify the legitimacy of enumerators by scanning the codes on their ID cards. The first phase of the digital census, which began on April 1, aims to cover over 30 lakh households across India. Residents are legally obligated to answer Census-related questions, and while there have been no cases of FIRs for non-response, local authorities will be involved in encouraging participation.  The second phase of the census, focusing on caste enumeration, is scheduled for February 2027.

recent_articles.title: Facing opposition, Ladakh administration says ‘stakeholders will be onboard on setting up a power corporation’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Union Territory (UT) administration** officials in Ladakh have stated that they are committed to involving local stakeholders in any decision regarding the establishment of a power corporation. **Ashish Kundra**, Chief Secretary of Ladakh, clarified that this move is mandated by the Electricity Act, 2003, and aims to generate revenue for the region.  He assured the public that existing employees will remain government employees while future recruitments will be handled by the corporation. The administration also emphasized its commitment to protecting Ladakh's land and culture, stating there are no plans to disturb the Changtang region or disrupt traditional employment practices.

recent_articles.title: Gurugram gated societies not letting in enumerators; FIRs recommended against enumerators obstructing Census work - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Haryana** administration has recommended an FIR against two government school staff for alleged negligence in Census-related work and obstruction of duties.  **Gurugram Municipal Corporation Joint Commissioner Punit Kumar** stated that enumerators have been denied entry into several highrise apartment buildings, prompting him to write to RWAs to ensure their access. **Registrar General of India Mritunjay Kumar Narayan** flagged off awareness vans across Delhi for the ongoing Census 2027 public outreach campaign.  The first phase of the Census began on April 1 and will conclude by September 30, involving around 30 lakh enumerators.

recent_articles.title: Nepal stirs row with India, objects to Kailash Mansarovar yatra via Lipulekh; MEA replies - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nepal** objected to **India** and **China's** plan to use the Lipulekh Pass for the upcoming Kailash Mansarovar Yatra, claiming it passes through their territory. The **Nepalese** government reiterated its long-standing position on the disputed region, stating that Limpiyadhura, Lipulekh, and Kalapani are integral parts of Nepal based on the 1816 Treaty of Sugauli.  The **Nepalese** Ministry of Foreign Affairs has formally informed both **India** and **China** of its stance and urged them to refrain from any activities in the area. **India**, however, maintains that the Lipulekh Pass route has been used for decades and rejects **Nepal's** territorial claims. The **Indian** External Affairs Ministry stated that it remains open to dialogue with **Nepal** on outstanding boundary issues.

recent_articles.title: Make right to vote a fundamental right, says Congress - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** general secretary Jairam Ramesh called for the right to vote to be made a fundamental right, arguing that it is currently not justiciable. He criticized the **Election Commission of India (ECI)** and its current leadership, alleging irregularities in electoral rolls and a lack of transparency.  Ramesh also expressed skepticism towards exit polls, citing their inaccuracy in previous elections. Meanwhile, **Rahul Gandhi** shared a video highlighting concerns from a delegation from Ladakh regarding suppression of democratic rights and land grabs by powerful individuals.

recent_articles.title: Piprahwa relics of Buddha arrive in Leh, people gather in huge numbers to pay respect - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: On Wednesday, April 29, 2026, the sacred Piprahwa relics of the Buddha arrived in Leh, Ladakh, for a public exposition. **Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena** accorded a ceremonial welcome to the relics at the Technical Area of Leh airport after they were flown in from New Delhi. The relics, linked to Gautama Buddha and discovered at Piprahwa, Uttar Pradesh, have gained renewed global significance after repatriation from a British family and private collection. **Khamtak Rinpoche**, **Rigyal Rinpoche**, and other religious figures were present at the reception ceremony.  The relics will be on display at Jivetsal in Leh from May 1 to May 10 before being taken to Zanskar and then back to Delhi.

recent_articles.title: Two Kashmir brothers: One killed by rebels, another by army 26 years later | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Mughal family in Kashmir is grappling with the deaths of their two sons, Ishfaq and Rashid, who were killed by rebels and the Indian army respectively.  **Rashid**, a commerce graduate, was shot dead by the army during an operation, while **Ishfaq**, a former army worker, was killed by rebels years earlier. The family believes both killings are part of a pattern of extrajudicial killings in Kashmir, where human rights groups have documented numerous cases of alleged abuses by security forces. Despite investigations ordered by authorities, no one has been held accountable for the deaths.  The Mughal family continues to demand justice and closure for their sons' deaths, while experts warn that impunity within the Indian military system perpetuates such tragedies.

recent_articles.title: Kashmir seminary declared unlawful under Indian law, sparks outcry | Religion News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: An important Islamic seminary in Indian-administered Kashmir, Jamia Siraj-ul-Uloom, has been declared unlawful under anti-terror laws.  **Kashmir Divisional Commissioner Anshul Garg** issued the order based on a police dossier alleging links to the banned political party Jamaat-e-Islami (JeI). **Mohammad Shafi Lone**, the seminary chairman, rejected the allegations and called the move a “calculated dismantling of Kashmir’s civic life.” Leaders in Muslim-majority Kashmir criticized the decision as part of an ongoing campaign of overreach by New Delhi.

recent_articles.title: Ladakh groups seek meeting with Shah and steps to build trust - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Ahead of **Amit Shah**, the **Union Home Minister**,’s visit to Ladakh, the **Leh Apex Body** (LAB) urged for a trust-building exercise and requested a meeting with him during his two-day tour. The LAB, composed of socio-political-religious organizations, also called for the convening of a high-powered committee, chaired by **Shah**, which includes members from the LAB and the Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA).

recent_articles.title: Union government to resume talks on Ladakh on May 22, 2026 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Vinai Kumar Saxena**, the **Ladakh Lieutenant-Governor**, announced the resumption of talks between the **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** and civil society bodies, the **Leh Apex Body** and the **Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA)** on May 22nd. This announcement follows a stalemate after violence erupted in Leh last year and comes ahead of a visit by **Union Home Minister Amit Shah** to Ladakh. The talks aim to address the core demands of civil society groups, including Statehood and inclusion under the Sixth Schedule, which are pursued by the **LAB** and **KDA**.

recent_articles.title: Children with Special Needs from State-run schools in Andhra Pradesh scale Everest Base Camp, set national benchmark - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Twenty-one children with special needs** from government schools in Andhra Pradesh successfully completed the Everest Base Camp trek in Nepal. The 16-day expedition, organized by **Samagra Shiksha**, Andhra Pradesh, and supported by the School Education Department, marked the first government-sponsored Everest Base Camp trek for specially-abled students.  The students, accompanied by mountaineers and officials, demonstrated their determination to overcome social stigma and achieve their goals. **Nara Lokesh**, HRD Minister and IT Minister of Andhra Pradesh, congratulated the students on their success and highlighted the importance of inclusivity in education.

recent_articles.title: Vehicles stranded after avalanche hits Srinagar-Kargil highway - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A snow avalanche on the **Kashmir-Ladakh** national highway caused significant disruptions, stranding several vehicles and leaving one driver missing. The incident occurred near Shaitan Nallah in Sonamarg, Kashmir, where a major avalanche swept into the highway, forcing its closure.  Rescue teams are actively searching for the missing driver while authorities have relocated stranded commuters to safer locations. This follows a similar tragedy on March 28th when seven people lost their lives in an avalanche at the Zojila Pass.

recent_articles.title: Pahalgam, a year on: Resilience falters, tourism struggles - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The 2025 attack on the Baisaran meadow in Pahalgam, Kashmir, has significantly impacted tourism and livelihoods. The incident resulted in the closure of several tourist destinations, including Baisaran, Dabyan, and Chandanwari, leading to job losses for locals who relied on tourism-related businesses.  **The Jammu and Kashmir Cable Car Corporation (JKCCC)** is planning a cable car project connecting the meadow with the Yatri Niwas hotel to attract pilgrims during the Amarnath Yatra. Security measures have been intensified in Pahalgam, including facial recognition technology at tourist destinations. The attack has also led to a decline in tourism footfall and financial hardship for hotels and businesses that relied on the influx of visitors.  **Mehraj Din Wani**, an ATV owner, expressed concerns about the long-term impact on local livelihoods.

recent_articles.title: Pahalgam terror attack: Govt appoints Karambir Singh Nalwa as Special Public Prosecutor to lead trial - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Centre** appointed noted lawyer **Karambir Singh Nalwa** as Special Public Prosecutor to lead the trial in the Pahalgam terror attack case, which claimed 25 tourists and a local pony operator's lives on April 22, 2025. The NIA filed a comprehensive chargesheet against six individuals and two terrorist organizations, Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba and its shadow outfit TRF, for their role in planning and executing the attack.  The agency traced the conspiracy to Pakistan, which it said has been "unabatedly sponsoring terrorism against India." The NIA named **Hafeez Saeed**, leader of **Lashkar-e-Taiba**, and **Habibullah Malik alias Sajid Jatt**, head of **The Resistance Front**, as accused in the chargesheet.

recent_articles.title: Two U.S. citizens detained at Srinagar airport over satellite-based GPS device - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Jammu and Kashmir police** detained two U.S. citizens at Srinagar airport on Sunday, April 19, 2026, after finding a GPS device in their travel bag. The **police** are investigating the matter, which involved a Garmin GPS device that can be operated from a satellite. One of the individuals was released as no evidence was found on him, while the other remains under investigation.

recent_articles.title: Consolidated voters’ list of 9 States and 3 UTs that underwent SIR Phase II trimmed by 10.2% - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission of India** announced the results of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in nine states and three Union Territories. **Uttar Pradesh** recorded the highest net deletion of voters at 2.04 crore, followed by **West Bengal**, with a net deletion of 83.86 lakh. The SIR phase II identified 67 lakh deceased voters and 1.28 crore duplicate voters across these states and UTs.  The consolidated electoral rolls saw a reduction of 10.2%, bringing the number of active voters down to 45.81 crore.

recent_articles.title: India rejects China’s ‘mischievous attempts’ to assign ‘fictitious’ names to places in Arunachal Pradesh - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India**'s Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) strongly condemned **China**'s recent creation of new counties in Xinjiang province, calling the actions "mischievous" and detrimental to bilateral relations.  The MEA stated that these attempts at assigning fictitious names to territories within India's territory detract from efforts to normalize ties and undermine understanding between the two nations. The ministry reiterated that Arunachal Pradesh is an integral part of **India** and will remain so.

recent_articles.title: Census of springs: 63.4% of springs in Kerala are under private ownership - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Union Jal Shakti Ministry** released the first Spring Census Report, which revealed that 63.4% of springs in Kerala are under private ownership, significantly higher than other states like Karnataka and Tamil Nadu where public ownership dominates.  The report, covering Kerala, Karnataka, Ladakh, Sikkim, Tamil Nadu, and Bihar, found that while Kerala has a high percentage of privately owned springs, the majority of springs across all surveyed states are publicly owned. The census, conducted by the **Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation**, aimed to inventory and map these critical water sources in response to depletion concerns.

recent_articles.title: Consolidated voters’ list of 12 States and UTs that underwent SIR Phase II trimmed by 10.2% - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission of India** announced the results of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which saw a significant reduction in voter numbers across nine states and three Union Territories. **Uttar Pradesh** recorded the highest net deletion of voters at 2.04 crore, followed by West Bengal with 83.86 lakh.  The revision identified 67 lakh deceased voters and 1.28 crore duplicate voters for removal. The consolidated electoral rolls across these regions saw a reduction of 10.2%, bringing the number of active voters down to 45.81 crore.

recent_articles.title: China sets up new county near PoK, Afghan border to curb Uyghur infiltration - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **China** has established a new county named Cenling in its Xinjiang region, near Pakistan-occupied Kashmir and Afghanistan. The move comes amid ongoing tensions with **India** over disputed territories, particularly in Ladakh.  The county will be administered by the Kashgar prefecture and is strategically significant due to its proximity to contested regions and the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor. Experts believe this development reflects China's recognition of the region's strategic importance and its efforts to strengthen local governance in border areas.

recent_articles.title: States to be pushed for ‘utility led aggregation’ to meet PM Surya Ghar targets - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)** is seeking to boost the adoption of its **PM Surya Ghar** program, which aims to provide solar energy access to one crore households by March 2027. The MNRE is encouraging states to adopt a “utility-led aggregation (ULA)” model where electricity distribution companies will pay for rooftop solar installations in eligible households.  The program has seen limited uptake but the MNRE is proposing incentives to increase participation. Despite this, India's renewable energy growth was significant in 2025-26, adding 55.3 gigawatts of non-fossil capacity, with solar power accounting for 44.6 GW.

recent_articles.title: Assembly elections 2026: ECI may roll out SIR in remaining 17 States, 5 UTs post polls - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission** is considering rolling out the third and final phase of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) for voters' lists in 22 states and Union territories after the Assembly elections this month. The exercise, which aims to clean up electoral rolls, could begin after the polls conclude on April 29th or after the declaration of results.  The **Election Commission** has already conducted SIR in 10 states and three Union Territories, covering nearly 60 crore voters.

recent_articles.title: ISRO launches Mission MITRA in Ladakh for astronaut study: Inside the 3,500m experiment testing human survival in space-like conditions | - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **ISRO**, the Indian Space Research Organisation, launched the Mission MITRA project to study crew behavior and performance in simulated space flight environments. The project, located in Leh, Ladakh, involves participants experiencing hypoxia, cold, and isolation, mirroring conditions found in space travel. **ISRO** is collaborating with the Institute of Aerospace Medicine in the Indian Air Force and other organizations to understand teamwork dynamics, communication skills, and physiological responses under stress. This research aims to inform the Gaganyaan human spaceflight program by providing insights into astronaut behavior and developing guidelines for crew composition and mission preparation.

recent_articles.title: Sonam Wangchuk gets warm welcome in Kargil, calls for unity and equal rights for Ladakh - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sonam Wangchuk**, a climate activist, was welcomed in Kargil on Sunday (April 5, 2026) after his release from jail.  He called for unity across Ladakh and the country while reiterating demands for democratic rights and constitutional protections for the region. **Leaders of Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA)** and **Leh Apex Body (LAB)** urged continued dialogue with the High Powered Committee, warning against delays in addressing their demands. Wangchuk emphasized the importance of unity and a shared sense of being Indian to achieve a better future.  **Haneefa Jan**, an MP, called for sincere government engagement and cautioned against using dialogue as a delaying tactic.

recent_articles.title: Several minority scholarship schemes discontinued after 2021-22, Minority Affairs Mister tells Rajya Sabha - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kiren Rijiju**, the **Minority Affairs Minister**, informed the Rajya Sabha that several scholarship schemes for minority students were discontinued after 2021-22.  Payments made in 2022-23 related to pending liabilities, and the government highlighted that these students are still covered under broader schemes like the PM-USP Yojana and the Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. The number of beneficiaries declined significantly after 2021-22, with some scholarships merged or limited to specific classes.  **John Brittas**, a CPI-M MP from Kerala, criticized the government's poor utilization of funds allocated for minority welfare.

recent_articles.title: Several minority scholarship schemes discontinued after 2021-22, Minority Affairs Mister tells Rajya Sabha - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Ministry of Minority Affairs** has discontinued several scholarship schemes for minority students beyond the 2021-22 academic year.  Responding to a question in Rajya Sabha, **Minority Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju** stated that pre-matric, post-matric, and merit-cum-means scholarships were not approved for continuation after 2021-22. The government highlighted that minority students continue to be covered under broader schemes like the PM-USP Yojana and the Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.  However, data shows a significant decline in beneficiaries and spending on these programs since 2021-22.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027 kicks off: How to do self-enumeration: step-by-step guide - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India's** Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner will conduct the 2027 census, a massive administrative and statistical exercise that collects demographic data on the entire country. The self-enumeration facility allows citizens to provide their household information online before enumerators visit, offering flexibility in filling out the census schedule.  The dates for self-enumeration vary by state and union territory, with most starting in April 2026. Census data is expected to be published within 2027 due to the digital nature of the process.

recent_articles.title: 55,000 households use Census self-enumeration portal on day one - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **President Droupadi Murmu**, **Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan**, **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, and **Union Home Minister Amit Shah** were among the first to use the online self-enumeration portal for the 2027 Population Census in eight States and Union Territories. The portal, which launched on April 1, 2026, allows households to provide information about their housing conditions and assets before enumerators visit.  The first phase of the census, focusing on house listing operations and housing census (HLO), will run until May 15th in these areas. Data collected through self-enumeration is confidential and will be used for evidence-based planning and policy formulation.

recent_articles.title: 7 killed as avalanche hits Srinagar-Leh National Highway - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: An avalanche struck the Zojila Pass in Kashmir, India, on Friday, March 27, 2026, burying several vehicles and leaving at least seven people dead. **Ladakh Lieutenant-Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena** directed relief efforts and deployed disaster relief forces while **Union Minister Jitendra Singh** expressed condolences to the families of those lost. The highway connecting Kashmir and Ladakh was closed for traffic.
